identification: Timber crate of old hand tools. Loose (photos 1-4): (1) cast iron cabinet scraper, sole cast 'No 12', two rosewood-type handles, brass thumbscrew, curved sole: Stanley No.12 veneer/cabinet scraper pattern (12 not 12 1/4 or 12 1/2 going by the casting); (2) duplex rebate/fillister plane with fence rod and depth stop, japanned, scale on fence arm: Stanley No.78 pattern; (3) small nickel/japanned block plane with brass front knob and brass rear adjuster, label on the lever cap (unreadable): Stanley/Record 9 1/2 type adjustable-mouth block plane; (4) small swivel-base engineer's bench vice, about 60-75 mm jaws, no name seen. In the crate (photo 5): Bailey-pattern bench plane, about No.4/5 size, wood knob and tote (maker unread); a second rusty cast plane/body; green-handled file/scraper; a cast tool with letters ending '...FORD' (possibly a saw set or clamp, unread); tinsnips, pliers, metal brackets, odds.
